title: AI stock rout deepens, with Anthropic hitting $74
html:
AI-linked stocks were hammered for a second straight day on Wednesday, with investor concern about rising costs and forbidding debt dynamics sending the shares of many of the industry’s largest players tumbling to fresh 52-week lows.

AI lab Anthropic traded as low as US$73.85 shortly after the open, putting it 11-per-cent below its initial offering price last week. Alphabet dropped 4.7 per cent and hit a 52-week low that was some 35-per-cent below its level at midyear. Chip giant Broadcom, one of the leaders of an epic midyear semiconductor rally, dropped 5.8 per cent and hit a 52-week low that left it 41-per-cent below its high for 2026.

The rout partly reflected the unwind of earlier optimism in the AI sector, driven in part by Democratic wins in U.S. midterm elections that promise greater regulation and a slower, costlier AI build out. Sentiment was further impaired on Wednesday by the Trump administration’s proposed new tariffs on imports from 14 trading partners and data showing US inflation increased further in October.

But the selling, which began soon after the Nasdaq composite’s record high on Oct. 6 and increased markedly in the second half of November, also underscored gathering concern about the financial underpinnings of an infrastructure expansion that has increasingly been financed by large sales of debt – a practice that tends to make markets more fragile and vulnerable to reversal.

Overnight in Tokyo, OpenAI shareholder SoftBank fell 14 per cent, underscoring fears that ChatGPT maker OpenAI may face increasing resistance as it seeks to raise money. SoftBank, also a major investor in chip firm Arm, is down more than 40 per cent for the year.

Nvidia, a major OpenAI partner in data centres and other aspects of the AI ecosystem, dropped 8.5 per cent to a fresh low. The so-called neocloud firms that back AI data centre capacity were under renewed attack, reflecting in part concern about their capacity to raise funds to support ambitious building plans.

“It seems that these companies are trying to one-up each other on the amount of money that they’re spending, but you have to show that it’s worth it, and that’s where Wall Street is saying ’I don’t know’,” said Todd Schoenberger, chief investment officer at CrossCheck Management.

Heading into bear territory

The Nasdaq-100 was down 4 per cent by mid-morning. The index briefly fell 20 per cent below its Oct. 6 record closing high, a level that would confirm a bear market if it held through Wednesday’s close.

The worries about the underpinnings of the AI boom were so significant that even firms reporting strong results were caught in the downdraft, reflecting in part their large stock-price gains earlier in the year. Dell Technologies fell 5.7 per cent on Wednesday despite the server maker raising its annual revenue and profit forecasts for the third time this year and approving an additional $25 billion share buyback. Dell stock has more than doubled for the year.

Rival AI server maker HPE tumbled 16.3 per cent on Tuesday after raising its full-year revenue outlook. Shares of Ambarella , valued at $2 billion, tumbled 20.9 per cent after the AI semiconductor firm forecast fourth-quarter revenue below analysts’ estimates.

The Philadelphia chips index slid 7 per cent to hit a more than seven-month low. The index has plunged more than 43 per cent from its record high in June. Shares of AI hyperscalers were broadly lower, with Oracle down 8 per cent and Amazon.com off 6 per cent.

Nvidia-backed neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius Group fell more than 10 per cent each, while IREN, Applied Digital and Core Scientific lost between 6.9 per cent and 10.8 per cent.

Neocloud providers, which rent out specialized AI computing capacity, have been under pressure since October over concerns about the debt funding their rapid expansion.

The yield on CoreWeave’s bonds due 2031 rose to almost 18 per cent as prices fell nearly 2 cents on the dollar to near record lows, Tradeweb data showed.

The cost of insurance against tech companies defaulting on debts has jumped sharply, with five-year CDS spreads at Oracle, Alphabet, SpaceX and CoreWeave hitting record levels.
summary: Shares of chipmakers, server makers and data-centre operators fell, while proposed new U.S. tariffs weighed on broader sentiment
